newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria frees 37 detainees held without charge.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria frees 37 detainees held without charge.

text.p: Thirty-seven detainees in Nigeria were freed after being held for up to 10 years without charge, the human rights group that handled their cases said on Wednesday.
The Constitutional Rights Project (CRP) said all 37 were released in December on "compassionate grounds" after being in detention for between three to 10 years without formal charges filed in court.

"The freed persons were in police custody for offences ranging from petty theft, suspected armed robbery and murder to vandalisation of equipment of NITEL and NEPA (state-run phone and electricity companies)," said Sonny Onyegbula, head of the CRP's legal department.

More than half of the 55,000 inmates of Nigerian prisons are people on remand awaiting trial, interior minister Baba Gana Kingibe said at a meeting of prison officials in the capital Abuja about this time last year.
Civil rights campaigners have long complained of congestion in Nigerian prisons and sought quicker prosecution of cases and more liberal terms for bail.

"Our legal department provides free services to the less- priviledged and victims of human rights abuses after we discover that people are arrested and detained for long periods by the police and may not be charged in court," Onyegbula said.
Military-ruled Nigeria has been under fire from home as well as from the international community for alleged human rights abuses arising from detentions without trial of its opponents.
Though some were freed last year many opposition figures are still held among them Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of an annulled 1993 presidential election.
